x2 — ~/i/x2. Realtime chat: SvelteKit app + a separate Cloudflare Worker at ws/ holding the Durable Objects.

TWO ROOTS, ONE COMMAND. Paths starting `src/` are the SvelteKit app. Paths starting `ws/src/` are the worker (ChatHub, Room, CreditAccount, and the Conv DO this plan adds). You always run commands from ~/i/x2; `pnpm test` is `vitest run` and its node project already includes BOTH `src/**` and `ws/**`, so one command covers everything. There is no package.json inside ws/.

STYLE (not optional): snake_case for every var and function; single-letter keys for stored payloads, request/response JSON and page-load return values; single-character stored enum values; no comments in code; Svelte 5 runes only ($props/$state/$derived/$effect/$bindable), never `export let`; all UI text lowercase; Tailwind utilities only, tokens from src/app.css, no raw hex/rgb/px; forms submit on Ctrl/Cmd+Enter only. Never start the dev server.

PRE-EXISTING BASELINE — DO NOT CHASE IT. `pnpm check` reports 15 errors and 31 warnings on a clean tree, and `pnpm lint` complains about formatting across ~84 files. Both predate this plan. The gate runs `plan/check_baseline.sh`, which fails only if the error count goes ABOVE 15. Never run `pnpm format` — it sweeps the whole repo and buries your change in 85 files of cosmetic churn. Format only what you touched: `pnpm exec prettier --write <the files you edited>`.

QDRANT IS BEING NARROWED, NOT REMOVED. After this plan Qdrant holds users (`s:'u'`) and groups (`s:'g'`) only — the two things with real vectors and real semantic search (people search on /app, room search on /app/rooms). Messages move to per-conversation Durable Objects. Thread search was already removed; cross-chat search was dropped. That is exactly what makes the single-copy message design possible.

TWO TRAPS THAT BITE SILENTLY:
- `src/lib/server/qdrant.ts` READS swallow errors into `[]` (`.catch(() => [])`), so "no results" and "Qdrant is down" look identical. `src/lib/server/hub_client.ts` does the OPPOSITE on purpose — it THROWS ChatHubError('network'|'http_<status>'|'bad_shape') so /app/chats can show an "unavailable" banner instead of a lying "no conversations yet". Any new DO read helper follows hub_client's throw-don't-swallow contract, never qdrant.ts's.
- NEVER add `wrangler types` to the `build` script; keep `build` as bare `vite build`. `pnpm gen` is known to fail here because worker-configuration.d.ts is hand-rolled.

Copy it with the `cp` the step gives — do not type it out, do not open it to "check" it, do not adapt an import that looks wrong. The gate byte-compares every placed test against the staged copy, so one altered character fails the step, and it keeps failing, because the fix is the implementation and never the test.

snapshot_script.s:
GIVE QDRANT A SECOND COPY AND A PROVEN RESTORE. This is the highest-value step in the plan; everything else is optimisation.
CURRENT STATE (verified live this session against the cluster in .env): `GET /collections/x2live` returns `"shard_number":1,"replication_factor":1`, and `GET /collections/x2live/snapshots` returns `{"result":[]}`. One node, one copy, zero backups ever taken. A single disk failure loses every user, message, room and folder. The collection currently holds 197 points, so a restore is trivially fast today and will not be later.
DO THIS:
  a. Write scripts/snapshot-qdrant.mjs (plain node, no deps beyond what the repo has; mirror the style of the existing scripts/backfill-conv-index.mjs which already reads QDRANT_URL/QDRANT_KEY from the environment). It must: POST `${QDRANT_URL}/collections/x2live/snapshots` with header `api-key: ${QDRANT_KEY}`; read `result.name` from the JSON response; GET `${QDRANT_URL}/collections/x2live/snapshots/${name}` to download the body; PUT it to R2 under key `qdrant/x2live/${new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)}.snapshot`; then DELETE the server-side snapshot so the cluster disk does not fill. Support `--dry-run` exactly like backfill-conv-index.mjs does.
  b. Wire it to the cron that already exists. ws/wrangler.jsonc has `"triggers": { "crons": ["*/1 * * * *"] }` and ws/src/index.ts's `scheduled()` handler already calls back into the main worker at `/api/cron/dispatch-scheduled` with `authorization: Bearer ${SECRET}`. Add a sibling route src/routes/api/cron/snapshot/+server.ts guarded by the identical `get_secret(env.SECRET)` bearer check that src/routes/api/cron/dispatch-scheduled/+server.ts uses, and have ws/src/index.ts's scheduled() hit it only when the current UTC hour and minute are both 0 (the cron fires every minute; gate inside the handler rather than adding a second cron expression).
  c. RESTORE DRILL — this is not optional and is the actual deliverable. Create a scratch collection, restore yesterday's snapshot into it via Qdrant's snapshot-recover API, and assert its points_count matches. A backup nobody has restored is a rumour, not a backup. Write down in the step's commit message what the restore actually took.
  d. Raise `replication_factor` to 2. This needs >=2 nodes on the Qdrant Cloud cluster, so it is a billing/tier change in the Qdrant dashboard, NOT a code change — and it CANNOT be applied to an existing collection in place; it requires creating a new collection with the new setting and migrating. If the tier upgrade is not happening now, SKIP 3(d) and say so explicitly in the commit — 3(a)-(c) alone move you from 'lose everything' to 'lose at most one day', which is the bulk of the value.
TRAP: point IDs in this collection MUST be a UUID or unsigned integer (a string with letters is rejected 400 'not a valid point ID'), and the collection runs strict_mode so filtering on an unindexed payload key is rejected outright — neither affects snapshots, but will bite if you hand-write any verification query.
GATE: `pnpm test` green (add a unit test for the snapshot script's URL/key construction using a fetch mock, in the style of src/lib/server/__tests__/push.test.ts), plus the drill evidence.

The restore drill and the replication_factor decision are the NEXT step, not this one. This step ships the script, the route and the cron gate only.

user_empty_vector.s:
STOP STORING 16 KB OF ZEROS PER USER. `ZV` is `new Array(4096).fill(0)` (src/lib/server/qdrant.ts). Qdrant holds vectors in RAM — the live collection config shows `"hnsw_config":{...,"on_disk":false}` — so every user with no profile text costs 16 KB of RAM to store nothing. The named_vector_migration already made this free to fix: a point may omit its vector entirely with `vector: {}` at zero storage and zero index cost, which is exactly what messages already do in send_msg().
FOUR SITES, all currently writing a full zero vector:
  src/lib/server/user.ts:54 in save_user() — `{ id, vector: { [V]: ZV }, payload: u as unknown as Record<string, unknown> }`
  src/lib/server/user.ts:102 in patch_user() — `vector: pt!.vector ?? { [V]: ZV },`
  src/lib/server/user.ts:124 in create_pw_user() — `{ id, vector: { [V]: ZV }, payload: u as unknown as Record<string, unknown> }`
  src/lib/server/profile.ts:66 in save_profile() — `{ id: uid, vector: { [V]: vec }, payload: merged ... }` where the line above it is `const vec = text ? await embed_text(env, text) : ZV;`
REPLACEMENT: at user.ts:54 and user.ts:124 write `vector: {}`. At user.ts:102 write `vector: pt!.vector ?? {}`. At profile.ts, restructure to `const vec = text ? await embed_text(env, text) : null;` and then `vector: vec ? { [V]: vec } : {}` — a user who clears their about/interests should DROP their vector, not keep a stale one, so do not just guard the write.
WHY `{}` and not a bare array or a smaller vector: this collection uses NAMED vectors (`V = 't'`), so a bare unnamed array is rejected 400 'Not existing vector name', and the vector size is fixed at 4096 by the collection config so a shorter array is also rejected. `{}` is the only zero-cost option and it is the documented purpose of the migration.
CONSEQUENCE TO CHECK: src/routes/api/search/+server.ts calls `search(env, vec, ...)` over `eq('s','u')`. Points with NO vector are invisible to vector search but still visible to `scroll()`. That endpoint already branches on `has_real_vec` and falls back to `scroll()` when the query is empty, so browsing still lists everyone; only semantic ranking skips profileless users — which is correct, they have no semantic content to rank on. Write a test that asserts exactly this so nobody 'fixes' it back later.
GATE: extend src/lib/server/__tests__/user.test.ts and profile.test.ts to assert the upsert payload's `vector` is `{}` in the no-profile case and `{ t: [...] }` in the with-profile case. `pnpm test` green, no new check/lint errors.

ws_reconnect_jitter.s:
ADD JITTER TO THE WEBSOCKET RECONNECT BACKOFF. src/lib/ws.ts:111 currently reads:
  `const delay = Math.min(30_000, 500 * 2 ** tries++);`
Every disconnected client therefore waits an IDENTICAL 500ms, then 1s, then 2s, then 4s. When a Cloudflare hiccup or a deploy drops many sockets at once, all of them reconnect on the same millisecond, the spike re-kills the thing that just recovered, they are all dropped again, and they all wait the same 1s. That is a self-sustaining outage that no amount of capacity fixes.
REPLACEMENT (keeps the same ceiling and the same growth curve, just spreads arrivals over the back half of each window):
  `const base = Math.min(30_000, 500 * 2 ** tries++);`
  `const delay = base / 2 + Math.random() * (base / 2);`
WHY full-jitter-over-half-window rather than `Math.random() * base`: the latter can fire almost immediately on every attempt, which defeats the backoff entirely on a struggling server. Half-window keeps a guaranteed minimum wait that still doubles, while making the arrival instant unpredictable.
TEST TRAP: src/lib/__tests__/ws.test.ts drives this module with fake timers and the module keeps state in module scope (`tries`, `timer`, `sock`) with a `_reset()` export for tests — call it in beforeEach. Stub randomness with `vi.spyOn(Math, 'random')` and assert two things: with random()=0 the delay equals base/2, and with random()→1 it approaches base; and that the ceiling still clamps at 30_000 after many tries. Do not assert an exact unjittered number anywhere.
GATE: `pnpm test` green.

hub_watch_fix.s:
FIX THE INVERTED WATCH HANDLER AND MAKE THE WATCHER FAN-OUT NON-BLOCKING — these must land together or fixing the first creates a worse bug.
BUG 1 (correctness, live today): src/routes/app/chat/[id]/+page.svelte builds `const watch = { type: 'watch', peer: data.peer };` and sends it to subscribe to a peer's presence. ws/src/hub.ts's webSocketMessage() handles it at the `} else if (msg.type === 'watch') {` branch by fetching `https://dummy/unwatch` (the call is around ws/src/hub.ts:239). So asking to watch UNSUBSCRIBES. Worse, the `/watch` route inside the same DO (the `if (url.pathname === '/watch' && request.method === 'POST')` block, around ws/src/hub.ts:115) is UNREACHABLE — ws/src/index.ts routes hub traffic through the regex `/^\\/hub\\/([^/]+)\\/(unread|read|mute|unmute|mutes|sub|unsub|convs|conv|sv)$/` which does not list `watch`, and nothing else fetches it. Net effect: the `watchers` array is permanently empty, `notify_watchers()` always iterates zero times, and live presence transitions NEVER push to anyone. The green dot only ever moves when the client explicitly sends `{ type: 'check' }`.
FIX 1: in webSocketMessage(), make `msg.type === 'watch'` fetch `https://dummy/watch`, and add a NEW branch `msg.type === 'unwatch'` that fetches `https://dummy/unwatch`. Then in src/lib/ws.ts / the chat page, send `{ type: 'unwatch', peer }` on teardown (the page already uses ws_drop/ws_send with the `keep` flag for handshake-persistent subscriptions — follow that existing pattern rather than inventing a new one).
BUG 2 (latent, becomes live the instant BUG 1 is fixed): notify_watchers() is a sequential `for (const watcher of watchers) { ... await stub.fetch(...) }`. It runs on EVERY socket open and EVERY socket close. A user with 200 watchers would do 200 serialized DO-to-DO round trips while holding their own DO's input gate, which stalls their incoming messages for the whole duration.
FIX 2: replace the loop body with `await Promise.all(watchers.slice(0, MAX_WATCHERS).map(async (watcher) => { try { ... } catch {} }))` and export `const MAX_WATCHERS = 200;` next to it. Also cap the array on the write side: the `/watch` route must refuse to grow `watchers` past MAX_WATCHERS (drop the oldest, or reject) — an unbounded array in DO storage is a slow leak.
WHY cap at all rather than just parallelising: DO subrequests are bounded per invocation (10,000 by default on paid, configurable), and an unbounded fan-out on every connect is a self-inflicted amplification. 200 is generous for a chat app's 'who am I watching' set.
GATE: ws/src/__tests__/hub-do.test.ts is the big existing suite for this DO — add cases there: (i) a `watch` message calls /watch not /unwatch; (ii) an `unwatch` message calls /unwatch; (iii) notify_watchers issues its fetches concurrently (assert all stubs were called before any resolve, using deferred promises); (iv) /watch refuses to exceed MAX_WATCHERS. `pnpm test` green.

Run `pnpm test` and watch it FAIL for the stated reason, then implement until it passes. Never edit it.

session_no_do_call.s:
STOP DOING A DURABLE OBJECT ROUND TRIP ON EVERY SINGLE HTTP REQUEST. src/hooks.server.ts:44 currently reads:
  `const sv = await hub_sv_get(env, x2_ws, s.user.id).catch(() => null);`
and it sits inside `handle`, which SvelteKit runs for every request — every page load, every /api/* call, every /media/* fetch. Each one blocks on a service-binding fetch to the x2-ws worker, which fetches that user's ChatHub DO, to read one integer (`sv`, the session version used by logout-all). The session cookie is already an HMAC-signed token (src/lib/server/session.ts, 7-day `e` expiry) — the entire point of a signed token is that it verifies locally with no I/O. This line throws that away and adds a network hop to one fixed datacenter on every request; a user far from that DO pays 100-300ms on EVERYTHING.
FIX (smallest that keeps logout-all working): delete the sv check from `handle` entirely. Instead call it only where a stale session actually matters:
  1. src/routes/api/wstoken/+server.ts — the websocket handshake. A revoked session must not get a fresh ws token. This is once per socket, not once per request.
  2. The credential-changing routes: src/routes/api/auth/set-password/+server.ts, src/routes/api/logout-all/+server.ts, src/routes/app/profile/+page.server.ts's actions.
Everywhere else, trust the signature. Worst case a revoked session keeps read access until its socket reconnects or the 7-day expiry lands.
EXTRACT the check into one exported helper (e.g. `assert_session_current(env, ws, user, v)` in src/lib/server/session.ts or hub_client.ts) that returns/throws consistently, so the three call sites cannot drift apart. Do NOT inline the same five lines three times.
IF INSTANT REVOCATION IS A HARD REQUIREMENT instead: shorten the cookie's `e` in encode_session() from `Date.now() + 604800000` (7 days) to ~15 minutes and refresh it in `handle` when it is close to expiry. Same guarantee, still zero per-request DO calls. Pick ONE of these two, do not do both.
TRAP: src/__tests__/hooks.server.test.ts currently asserts the sv behaviour — it is one of the files already modified in the working tree before this session, so read its current contents before editing and only change the sv-related cases. Also note `handle` currently branches on `if (session_id && x2_ws)` vs `else if (session_id)`; once the sv call is gone those two branches collapse into one, so simplify them rather than leaving a dead branch.
GATE: `pnpm test` green including updated hooks.server.test.ts and a new wstoken test proving a stale `v` is rejected there.

```

```
Run `pnpm test` and watch it FAIL for the stated reason, then implement until it passes. Never edit it.

When the step is done: `git add . && git commit` scoped to it, then `git push`. Do not run the gate yourself; `plan` runs it on mark.

hub_msg_table.s:
CREATE A PER-CONVERSATION DURABLE OBJECT WITH A SQLITE MESSAGE TABLE AND START DUAL-WRITING TO IT (Qdrant stays authoritative until migrate_msgs).
WHY PER-CONVERSATION AND NOT PER-USER: one copy of each message, not one per participant. Cloudflare bills rows written at $1.00/million and DO requests at $0.15/million, so duplicating a row costs ~6.7x more than an extra request. A DM costs 1 row + 1 request (~$1.15/M messages) instead of 2 rows (~$2.00/M); a 50-member group costs the SAME $1.15/M instead of $50/M, and 1x storage instead of 50x. It also makes edit/delete/reaction a single write instead of an N-way fan-out with a consistency problem, gives a newly-joined group member the full back-history for free, and puts the 10 GB per-DO cap on a conversation (which would need ~25M messages to fill) rather than on a user. There is NO search index — thread search was removed and cross-chat search was ditched, which is exactly what makes the single-copy design available.
DO THIS:
  a. New file ws/src/conv.ts exporting `class Conv implements DurableObject`. Model it on the existing ws/src/room.ts (same shape, same constructor signature) — that file is already a per-group DO, so the pattern is in-repo.
  b. In the constructor run `this.state.storage.sql.exec(...)` for:
     `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS m (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, f TEXT NOT NULL, t TEXT, gr TEXT, x TEXT, im TEXT, fl TEXT, rp TEXT, sk TEXT, rx TEXT, fw INTEGER, d INTEGER NOT NULL, e INTEGER);`
     `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS m_d ON m (d);`
     No `conv` column — the DO's own identity IS the conversation, so storing it in every row is dead weight. `fl` and `rx` hold JSON strings (they are objects on Message in src/lib/types.ts). `fw` is 0/1. Keep the single-letter key names; that is this repo's stored-payload convention.
  c. Routes on the DO: `POST /put` (INSERT OR IGNORE keyed on message id — relay is best-effort and IS retried, so a duplicate delivery must not create a second row), `GET /page?before=<ts>` (`SELECT * FROM m WHERE (?1 IS NULL OR d < ?1) ORDER BY d DESC LIMIT 50`), `POST /edit`, `POST /del`, `POST /react`.
  d. Register it in ws/wrangler.jsonc: add `{ \"name\": \"CONV\", \"class_name\": \"Conv\" }` to `durable_objects.bindings` AND a new migration entry `{ \"tag\": \"v6\", \"new_sqlite_classes\": [\"Conv\"] }`. Export it from ws/src/index.ts alongside `export { Room } from './room';`.
  e. Route to it in ws/src/index.ts. Copy the existing `/room/` branch verbatim as the template — it already does the bearer-secret check, splits the path, and forwards `${url.search}`. The DO id is `env.CONV.idFromName(conv)` where `conv` is the value src/lib/server/chat.ts's `conv_id(a,b)` (sorted `a|b`) or `group_conv_id(gid)` (`g:<gid>`) already produces. Do not invent a new id scheme.
  f. Call it from src/routes/api/send/+server.ts. Write to the Conv DO FIRST and let its success be what the 200 depends on (this replaces Qdrant's role as the durability point — /api/send currently turns an upsert failure into a 503 'not_stored', keep that behaviour pointed at the new write). The existing relay to each recipient's ChatHub still fires for delivery, unread and push and is unchanged.
DO NOT yet change any read path and DO NOT stop writing to Qdrant. This step must leave behaviour identical; it only starts filling the new table.
TRAP: Workers serializes concurrent fetch() calls to the same DO instance, so these read-modify-writes need no CAS — the same guarantee ws/src/credit_account.ts documents in its header comment. Do not add locking.
KNOWN CEILING (note it, do not build for it): a single DO has a soft threshold of ~1,000 requests/sec, so one extremely hot conversation serializes. That is a 10k-member live broadcast room. If it ever happens, shard by time bucket (`g:<gid>:2026-08`).
GATE: new ws/src/__tests__/conv.test.ts proving one relayed message lands exactly one row, a duplicate `put` lands exactly one row, `page` orders desc and honours `before`, and edit/del/react mutate correctly. `pnpm test` green.

TEST — already written, staged, and byte-compared by the gate. Copy it into place BEFORE implementing:
```
cp plan/tests/ws/src/__tests__/conv.test.ts.txt ws/src/__tests__/conv.test.ts
```
Run `pnpm test` and watch it FAIL for the stated reason, then implement until it passes. Never edit it.

When the step is done: `git add . && git commit` scoped to it, then `git push`. Do not run the gate yourself; `plan` runs it on mark.
hub_msg_table.t: test -f ws/src/conv.ts && grep -q "Conv" ws/wrangler.jsonc && grep -q "export { Conv }" ws/src/index.ts && bash plan/verify_tests.sh && pnpm test && bash plan/check_baseline.sh

hub_msg_reads.s:
SWITCH THE READ PATHS TO THE Conv DURABLE OBJECT, AND FIX THE ChatHub N+1 THAT REMAINS.
REPLACE THESE:
  a. src/lib/server/chat.ts's `page_msgs()` currently does `scroll(env, f(eq('s','m'), eq('c', conv)), PAGE, undefined, { key: 'd', direction: 'desc', start_from: before - 1 })` against Qdrant. Replace with a call to the Conv DO's `GET /page?before=<ts>`. KEEP the existing behaviour that the result is re-sorted ASCENDING before returning (page_msgs ends with `.sort((x, y) => x.d - y.d)`) — the client depends on it. Add the client helper next to the existing `room_join`/`room_members` helpers in src/lib/server/hub_client.ts, following their exact shape.
  b. `get_message()`, and the `retrieve_one` calls inside `edit_msg` / `delete_msg` / `toggle_reaction` in src/lib/server/chat.ts, all move to the Conv DO. THE AUTHORIZATION LOGIC MUST BE PRESERVED EXACTLY: edit_msg throws 'not author' unless `m.f === uid`; delete_msg additionally allows a group OWNER (it calls get_group and checks `g.owner !== uid`). Keep those checks in the Worker, not in the DO — the DO has no notion of who is asking.
  c. SEPARATELY, ChatHub keeps its own conversation index (the `conv:` and `unread:` keys) because that is what powers /app/chats, and it is still an N+1: `list_convs()` in ws/src/hub.ts lists all `conv:` keys then does TWO sequential storage gets per conversation (an `is_muted()` and an `unread:` lookup), and `unread_totals()` does the same and runs on EVERY incoming push. Because messages now live in the Conv DO, this index cannot be replaced by a GROUP BY — so fix it in place: read `storage.list({ prefix: 'mute:' })` and `storage.list({ prefix: 'unread:' })` ONCE each up front and join in memory. Three reads instead of 2N.
TRAP: src/lib/server/hub_client.ts's `hub_convs` deliberately THROWS ChatHubError('network'|'http_<status>'|'bad_shape') instead of returning [], because src/routes/app/chats/+page.server.ts must render an 'unavailable' banner rather than the misleading 'no conversations yet' empty state. Any new Conv read helper MUST follow that same throw-don't-swallow contract. This is the OPPOSITE of src/lib/server/qdrant.ts, whose reads swallow errors into [] — do not copy that pattern.
GATE: `pnpm test` green, including src/routes/app/chats/__tests__/page.server.test.ts (already asserts the banner), the chat page's history/pagination tests, and new ws/src/__tests__/hub-do.test.ts cases proving list_convs and unread_totals issue a constant number of storage reads regardless of conversation count.

TEST — already written, staged, and byte-compared by the gate. Copy it into place BEFORE implementing:
```
cp plan/tests/ws/src/__tests__/hub_index_reads.test.ts.txt ws/src/__tests__/hub_index_reads.test.ts
```
Run `pnpm test` and watch it FAIL for the stated reason, then implement until it passes. Never edit it.

When the step is done: `git add . && git commit` scoped to it, then `git push`. Do not run the gate yourself; `plan` runs it on mark.
hub_msg_reads.t: ! grep -q "scroll(env" src/lib/server/chat.ts && bash plan/verify_tests.sh && pnpm test && bash plan/check_baseline.sh

drop_msg_crypto.s:
REMOVE APPLICATION-LEVEL MESSAGE ENCRYPTION. Decision made deliberately: Durable Object storage is already AES-256 encrypted at rest by Cloudflare automatically (LUKS, no configuration), so the app-level layer mainly protected against a Qdrant-side breach — and messages are leaving Qdrant. What you give up: protection if Cloudflare itself is compromised. Accepted.
DO THIS:
  a. Delete src/lib/server/msg_crypto.ts and src/lib/server/__tests__/msg_crypto.test.ts.
  b. In src/lib/server/chat.ts remove `import { encrypt_text, decrypt_text } from './msg_crypto';` and every call. Currently: send_msg() and send_group_msg() both write `payload: { ...m, x: await encrypt_text(env, text) }`; edit_msg() writes `x: await encrypt_text(env, new_text)`; page_msgs(), get_message() (and formerly search_messages) map results through `decrypt_text`. All of these become plain `text` / plain `m.x`.
  c. Remove the `MESSAGE_ENC_KEY` entry from the `secrets_store_secrets` array in wrangler.jsonc, and `MESSAGE_ENC_KEY?: SecretVal;` from the `QEnv` type in src/lib/server/qdrant.ts.
  d. DO NOT delete the secret from the Cloudflare Secrets Store yet — migrate_msgs still needs it to decrypt the existing rows. Deleting it early makes every pre-existing `enc:` message permanently unreadable.
SEQUENCING IS THE WHOLE RISK HERE: this step must land BEFORE migrate_msgs for new writes, but the key must survive UNTIL migrate_msgs has run. If you would rather not hold that ordering in your head, merge this step into migrate_msgs and do it in one commit.
TRAP: decrypt_text currently swallows failures and RETURNS THE CIPHERTEXT (`catch { return stored; }`), which is why a bad key shows users literal `enc:AAAA...` text instead of an error. Do not reproduce that behaviour anywhere in the migration — there, a decrypt failure must be loud.
GATE: `pnpm test` green after deleting the crypto tests and updating every chat test that currently asserts on an `enc:` prefix.

When the step is done: `git add . && git commit` scoped to it, then `git push`. Do not run the gate yourself; `plan` runs it on mark.
drop_msg_crypto.t: test ! -f src/lib/server/msg_crypto.ts && ! grep -q "MESSAGE_ENC_KEY" src/lib/server/qdrant.ts && ! grep -q "MESSAGE_ENC_KEY" wrangler.jsonc && bash plan/verify_tests.sh && pnpm test && bash plan/check_baseline.sh

migrate_msgs.s: move existing messages into the conv durable objects

migration_script.s:
MOVE THE EXISTING MESSAGES INTO THE Conv DURABLE OBJECTS AND STOP WRITING MESSAGES TO QDRANT. The collection currently holds 197 points, of which 167 carry the `c` (conversation) payload index — so this is a tiny, fast, low-risk migration TODAY and will not stay that way.
DO THIS:
  a. Write scripts/migrate-msgs-to-conv.mjs in the style of the existing scripts/backfill-conv-index.mjs (same env-var reading, same `--dry-run` flag, same batching). It must: scroll Qdrant for `f(eq('s','m'))`; for each message DECRYPT `x` using MESSAGE_ENC_KEY if and only if it starts with `enc:` (legacy plaintext rows have no prefix — see the ponytail comment in msg_crypto.ts); then POST it to the Conv DO whose id is `m.c` (the payload already carries the exact conversation id — `a|b` for DMs, `g:<gid>` for groups — so no id derivation is needed). ONE destination per message, not one per participant. A DECRYPT FAILURE MUST ABORT THE WHOLE RUN LOUDLY, never write ciphertext through as if it were text.
  b. Run `--dry-run` first and eyeball the counts. Then run for real. Then VERIFY: pick several conversations and diff message count plus newest/oldest timestamps between Qdrant and the Conv DO before trusting it.
  c. Only after verification, remove the Qdrant message writes: in src/lib/server/chat.ts, send_msg() and send_group_msg() stop calling `upsert`; edit_msg/delete_msg/toggle_reaction stop calling upsert/remove/set_payload.
  d. src/lib/server/scheduled.ts stores ScheduledMessage records with `s: 'sm'` in Qdrant — those are NOT chat messages and STAY in Qdrant. Do not migrate them.
  e. Now delete MESSAGE_ENC_KEY from the Cloudflare Secrets Store (`wrangler secrets-store secret ...`). It is finally unused.
  f. Leave the message points in Qdrant untouched for at least one deploy cycle as a fallback, exactly as the named_vector_migration left the old `x2` collection in place. Delete them in a follow-up only once the Conv path has been live and healthy.
WHAT QDRANT KEEPS AFTER THIS: users (`s:'u'`) and groups (`s:'g'`) only — exactly the two things that still have vectors and still need semantic search (people search on /app, room search on /app/rooms). That is Qdrant doing the job it is actually good at.
TRAP: src/lib/server/qdrant.ts's READS swallow errors into [] (`.catch(() => [])`), so an empty scroll during migration can mean 'Qdrant unreachable', not 'no messages'. The migration script must NOT use those helpers — call the Qdrant REST API directly and fail loudly on any non-2xx.
GATE: `pnpm test` green; plus recorded before/after counts from the verification in (b).

This step writes and dry-runs the script ONLY. The real run, the verification diff, dropping the Qdrant writes and deleting MESSAGE_ENC_KEY are the next step — they touch live data.

When the step is done: `git add . && git commit` scoped to it, then `git push`. Do not run the gate yourself; `plan` runs it on mark.
migration_script.t: test -f scripts/migrate-msgs-to-conv.mjs && node scripts/migrate-msgs-to-conv.mjs --dry-run && bash plan/verify_tests.sh && pnpm test && bash plan/check_baseline.sh

run_and_cutover.s:
RUN THE MIGRATION FOR REAL, VERIFY IT, THEN STOP WRITING MESSAGES TO QDRANT.

1. Run scripts/migrate-msgs-to-conv.mjs for real. A DECRYPT FAILURE MUST ABORT THE WHOLE RUN LOUDLY — never write ciphertext through as if it were text.
2. VERIFY before trusting it: pick several conversations and diff message count plus newest/oldest timestamps between Qdrant and the Conv DO.
3. Only after verification, remove the Qdrant message writes in src/lib/server/chat.ts: send_msg() and send_group_msg() stop calling upsert; edit_msg/delete_msg/toggle_reaction stop calling upsert/remove/set_payload.
4. src/lib/server/scheduled.ts stores ScheduledMessage records with `s:'sm'` — those are NOT chat messages and STAY in Qdrant.
5. Now delete MESSAGE_ENC_KEY from the Cloudflare Secrets Store. It is finally unused.
6. Leave the message points in Qdrant untouched for at least one deploy cycle as a fallback. Delete them in a follow-up once the Conv path has been live and healthy.

THIS STEP IS NOT MACHINE-CHECKABLE AND NOT YOURS TO ATTEMPT. It rewrites live user data and deletes a production secret. If you are an unattended executor: run `plan lean_scale migrate_msgs.run_and_cutover --block "migration script ready and dry-run clean, live run pending"` immediately and stop. Do not mark it. Do not fake it.

signed_media_urls.s:
SERVE IMAGES FROM CACHEABLE SIGNED URLS INSTEAD OF PROXYING EVERY BYTE THROUGH A COOKIE-AUTHED WORKER.
CURRENT STATE: messages carry a bare R2 key and the client builds `/media/${key}` (src/lib/server/media.ts's `media_url()`, src/lib/attach.ts's `media_src()`, and src/routes/api/send/+server.ts which puts `image: /media/${image}` into the relay payload). src/routes/media/[...key]/+server.ts then takes the unsigned branch: `if (!locals.user) throw error(401, 'auth')`. Because the response depends on the caller's cookie, the CDN cannot cache it — so every view of every image re-runs a Worker and re-reads R2, even though the handler sets `cache-control: public, max-age=86400, immutable`.
Meanwhile `sign_key()` and `signed_media_url()` ALREADY EXIST in src/lib/server/media.ts and produce `/media/<key>?e=<exp>&s=<sig>`, which the same route already validates in its signed branch — and that path is currently DEAD CODE in the message flow. put_image() and put_file() even return a signed `url` that nothing uses.
DO THIS:
  a. Store/emit the SIGNED url in the message flow instead of the bare key — or, better, keep storing the bare key (it is the durable identifier) and sign at render time in the page loaders, so an expiry cannot be baked permanently into stored data. Prefer the render-time signing: the 24h expiry in put_image() is otherwise stale the moment a message is a day old.
  b. Then DELETE the cookie branch from src/routes/media/[...key]/+server.ts so the route is signature-only and unambiguously cacheable.
  c. Separately: `delete_image()` in src/lib/server/media.ts is never called by any route. src/routes/api/messages/[id]/delete/+server.ts calls delete_msg (which returns `media_key`) and ignores it, so deleting a message orphans its R2 object forever. Wire the deletion up in the same step.
TRAP: the r2_buckets binding in wrangler.jsonc is marked `"remote": true` so `wrangler dev` proxies to the real x2-media bucket; plain `pnpm dev` (bare vite) never touches R2 at all. Verify this against `pnpm dev:full`, not `pnpm dev`. Also noted in that config comment: the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in this environment lacks R2 read permission, so `wrangler r2 object get` cannot confirm an upload landed — verify through the app, not the CLI.
GATE: `pnpm test` green including src/routes/media/__tests__/server.test.ts updated to prove the cookie branch is gone and an unsigned request is rejected.

TEST — already written, staged, and byte-compared by the gate. Copy it into place BEFORE implementing:
```
cp plan/tests/src/routes/media/__tests__/signed_only.test.ts.txt src/routes/media/__tests__/signed_only.test.ts
```
Run `pnpm test` and watch it FAIL for the stated reason, then implement until it passes. Never edit it.

When the step is done: `git add . && git commit` scoped to it, then `git push`. Do not run the gate yourself; `plan` runs it on mark.
signed_media_urls.t: ! grep -q "locals.user" 'src/routes/media/[...key]/+server.ts' && grep -q "delete_image" src/routes/api/messages/'[id]'/delete/+server.ts && bash plan/verify_tests.sh && pnpm test && bash plan/check_baseline.sh

retention.s:
ADD RETENTION SO STORAGE STOPS GROWING FOREVER. Nothing in this app ever deletes anything: no message TTL, no R2 lifecycle rule, no archive tier. Storage cost is rate x time with no ceiling, and there is currently no mechanism to satisfy a GDPR deletion request.
WITH THE PER-CONVERSATION DESIGN the 10 GB per-DO cap applies to a single conversation. At roughly 400 bytes a row that is ~25 million messages in one chat, so the cap is not the driver here — cumulative cost across all conversations is. Note also that single-copy storage means retention now frees the full amount rather than 1/Nth of it.
DO THIS:
  a. In the Conv DO, add a `state.storage.setAlarm()` daily sweep running `DELETE FROM m WHERE d < ?` for a configurable cutoff. FROM THE DO PRICING DOCS: `setAlarm()` is billed as one row written and deletes are billed as rows written — a daily alarm is negligible, a per-message alarm would not be.
  b. Add an R2 lifecycle rule moving objects not accessed in N days to Infrequent Access. Bucket setting in the Cloudflare dashboard, zero code.
  c. DECIDE THE POLICY FIRST and write it down — keep forever, 1 year, or user-configurable. Product decision, not engineering. Read the number from one named constant, do not scatter it.
GATE: `pnpm test` green with a conv.test.ts case that seeds rows either side of the cutoff and asserts only the old ones are swept.

TEST — already written, staged, and byte-compared by the gate. Copy it into place BEFORE implementing:
```
cp plan/tests/ws/src/__tests__/conv_retention.test.ts.txt ws/src/__tests__/conv_retention.test.ts
```
Run `pnpm test` and watch it FAIL for the stated reason, then implement until it passes. Never edit it.

When the step is done: `git add . && git commit` scoped to it, then `git push`. Do not run the gate yourself; `plan` runs it on mark.
retention.t: grep -q "RETENTION_MS" ws/src/conv.ts && grep -q "setAlarm" ws/src/conv.ts && bash plan/verify_tests.sh && pnpm test && bash plan/check_baseline.sh

staging_and_metrics.s:
ADD A STAGING ENVIRONMENT AND FOUR NUMBERS. Right now wrangler.jsonc and ws/wrangler.jsonc each define ONE environment with `workers_dev: true`, so a deploy goes straight to real users, and `"observability": { "enabled": true, "head_sampling_rate": 0.01 }` samples 1% of logs into a place nobody looks.
DO THIS:
  a. Add an `env.staging` block to BOTH wrangler configs pointing at a SEPARATE Qdrant collection (not x2live) and a separate R2 bucket. Deploy there first, always.
  b. Instrument exactly four numbers and put them on one screen. Not a metrics platform — four numbers:
     - send success rate (did the message get stored: the only thing that truly matters)
     - delivery p99 (send -> other device)
     - hub error rate (ChatHubError by reason: network / http_<status> / bad_shape — the typed reasons already exist in src/lib/server/hub_client.ts)
     - Qdrant error rate (catches the failure mode where qdrant.ts's `.catch(() => [])` reads make an outage look like empty data)
     Use Workers Analytics Engine plus one dashboard panel. Do not build anything bespoke.
  c. Drop the per-call firehose log. src/lib/server/hub_client.ts's `call()` currently runs `console.log(\"[HUB] ${method} /hub/${uid.slice(0,8)}${path} -> ${res.status} ${ms}ms\")` on EVERY hub call. Make it error-only. At volume this log costs more than the compute it describes.
TRAP (repo-specific, do not skip): NEVER add `wrangler types` to the `build` script — keep `build` as `vite build` only. `pnpm gen` is already known to fail in this repo because worker-configuration.d.ts is hand-rolled; `wrangler types --check` also falsely reports it stale in Cloudflare Workers Builds. Also, the `WS_ORIGIN` var in wrangler.jsonc and `X2_ORIGIN`/`SECRET` in ws/wrangler.jsonc are committed deliberately: `wrangler deploy` OVERWRITES dashboard-set values with whatever the config says on every push, so a blank value silently re-breaks realtime delivery. Give staging its own real values, never blanks.
GATE: a staging deploy that serves traffic, and the four numbers visible on one screen.

THIS STEP IS NOT MACHINE-CHECKABLE AND NOT YOURS TO ATTEMPT. A staging deploy that serves traffic and four numbers on a dashboard cannot be proved by a shell command. If you are an unattended executor: run `plan lean_scale staging_and_metrics --block "everything else shipped, staging env and metrics pending"` immediately and stop.
